`binding/form.go` and `binding/query.go` just call `mapForm` from `form_mapping.go`. Since the question is about the implementation, `form_mapping.go` is the single most relevant file, with the other two being thin wrappers.

The core implementation lives in `binding/form_mapping.go` — `tryToSetValue`, `setByForm`, and `trySplit` handle copying request values onto struct members by tag name (falling back to the field name), applying `default=` fallback values from the tag options, and splitting list/array values on the `collection_format` delimiter (csv, ssv, tsv, pipes); the other binding files (`header.go`, `query.go`, `form.go`) reuse this same `formSource`/`TrySet` machinery for their respective request sources.

`binding/form_mapping.go` — This is the single file that implements the full mechanism: `tryToSetValue` resolves the tag name (falling back to the struct field name when the tag is empty), parses `default=` options for fallback values, and `setByForm`/`trySplit` handle slice/array members by splitting values on the `collection_format` delimiter (csv/ssv/tsv/pipes) or keeping them multi-valued.

`binding/form.go` — The form bindings (`formBinding`, `formPostBinding`) that collect `req.Form`/`req.PostForm` and call `mapForm`, which delegates to the mapping logic above.

`binding/query.go` — The query binding that collects `req.URL.Query()` and calls `mapForm` with the same underlying mapping.

`binding/multipart_form_mapping.go` — The multipart binding's `TrySet` implementation, which extends the same `setter` interface to handle `multipart.FileHeader` slices and falls back to `setByForm` for non-file fields.

`binding/mapping.go` — (if present) the recursive struct-walking entry point `mapping`/`mappingByPtr` that drives field traversal and calls `tryToSetValue`.
